system.summary: Homophonic substitution over Latin letters, digits and signs, in which some letter pairs are single units (m i, o o, l o, n o, p a, c c, d d, b b, l a, b o, m o, g r, g 1, b u); a few code signs (a boxed sign, H, IZ, a cross, a looped che-shaped sign) have no value. 54 units, 38 with a value.
system.notes: No key sheet, gloss or contemporary decipherment is known; every value is fitted from the text (grade S). The single o never stands alone, which is what showed the pair units. lo gives t in most words but l in five places with no graphic rule found.

prior_solution.where: No decipherment of any of the three leaves is known. For f. 68r, Benzoni (DBI 45, 1995) quotes three phrases of the episode ('orine' tinte di 'sangue', 'sano et gagliardo') and cites Vat. lat. 8214; the text he quotes from has not been found. His account was found by the Codex review after the reading (15 Nov 2026) and was not used to make it.

conditions.human_role: Contributed result (GitHub issue #697, Andrew Aymeloglu, 16 Nov 2026; work of 15 Nov): Claude Code agents (Claude Fable and Claude Opus) transcribed the three leaves, paged the volume for further cipher, annealed a key and refined it by hand word by word; Codex reviewed independently; the contributor reviewed the result. The project reran the files (issue #697).
tools: cipherkit (the contributor's annealer and controls; not included here)
aaymeloglu/verify.py (recomputes the key output and the tiers)

solution.what: All 816 images of Vat. lat. 8214 paged on DigiVatLib for cipher, glosses, clear copies or keys: cipher only on ff. 68r, 198r and 298r-v; no gloss, clear copy or key in the volume.
The three leaves transcribed sign by sign from the full-size IIIF images (1962 px), with alternatives x{y}? for doubtful signs; 68r second-checked on 5 of 23 lines.

Homophonic simulated annealing with a 4-gram Italian character model (cipherkit 'it' corpus) on the three leaves pooled; it did not converge until letter pairs were joined as single units (the single o never stands alone).

Lines 68r 20-23 set aside before the hand refinement, with scoring rules written in advance. The starting key had been fitted on all lines including these and their decode had been printed once, so this is a fit-consistency check with leakage, not a held-out test.

Values fixed by hand only where several independent words agree (Prospero, Carpi, heredi, investitura, Cremona, fatto, fiume, Februarii); further pair units added where repeated words required them (b u after the reserved count). Segments graded strict, forced, lenient, doubt, unread: 141, 22, 35, 11, 18 of 227.

Key shuffle on the fitted text (200 shuffles, reserved lines excluded): 4-gram z = 14.5; lexicon-string segments 81 of 191 against 19.0 +/- 5.9 (circular for a hand-tuned key). Reserved lines: 19 of 31 segments lexicon strings against 4.8 +/- 1.6; 10 of 20 fully keyed segments of 4+ letters against 0.06 (with the later b u unit and two image corrections, 22 of 31 and 13 of 20, reported apart). Leave-one-out: the 4-gram model returns the key value for most units but not for I, i, 6, b, pa, bu, bb, g1, o, S. Merges tested both ways: splitting l o or n o loses hits.

Matched synthetic control: an unaided anneal of f. 298 alone (406 units) recovered 35-60% of synthetic homophonic Italian of the same shape; at about 1,200 units and 38 symbols it recovered 94% in one run of three and 45% in two (on an earlier unit scheme).

Independent review by Codex: 174 signs in 19 key groups checked on the images, every key output and the control arithmetic reproduced, the historical claims checked (Benzoni's account of the urine deception found). Its corrections at 298v 04/6 and 68r 23/4, 23/5, the reading 've parira' and the historical corrections applied; 68r 19/2 kept against it (two signs visible on the image).

The project (issue #697): verify.py reproduces every count; an own decoder from key.json gives the key output for all 227 segments (1,197 units); the 298r and 198r image hashes match the BAV copies; the two cipher lines of 198r agree with the scan sign for sign. Count by the project's rule (strict segments read, all others holes): 50% of 284 cipher words (298r-v 38%, 68r 55%, 198r 79%).

Source of Benzoni's quotation from the 68r episode (DBI 45, 1995; his Fonti list Vat. lat. 8214, Castiglione's Lettere ed. Gorni 1969 and ed. La Rocca I 1978): neither edition found online (archive.org checked); one web search on the quoted phrases found nothing. Not found.

outcome.method_basis: No key sheet, gloss or decipherment is known; the key was fitted by annealing on the three leaves pooled and refined by hand from the words the text makes, with the clear text around the runs as context.
outcome.fraction_read_source: The project's count (issue #697 comment, 16 Nov 2026): only strict segments are read; forced, lenient, doubtful and unread segments are holes; 50% of 284 cipher words (298r-v 38%, 68r 55%, 198r 79%). Reproduced by aaymeloglu/running_text.py: 143 of 284 (37 of 98, 95 of 172, 11 of 14). With unread sign groups sized as one word each (the running texts' marks): 143 of 253 (56.5%). The contributor's segment counts: 141 of 227 strict.
outcome.notes: Work by Claude Code agents (Claude Fable, Claude Opus) with a Codex review; Andrew Aymeloglu reviewed. Every value is fitted from the text (grade S). The secure core: 298v and the urine passage of 68r are nearly all strict; 198r reads Cremona sign for sign. The one outside check is Benzoni's quotation for 68r, whose source has not been found.

texts.label: Suardino from the Imperial court, [Vitoria?], 26 February [1524], f. 298r-v
texts.summary: Suardino reports from Charles V's court on Carpi, granted to Prospero Colonna, who died in late December 1523, without the investiture: the grant stands for his heirs, though the Emperor might draw money from it for his needs in Italy and compensate the heirs otherwise; whether Carpi had been taken from Alberto Pio by right was still undetermined.

texts.label: A letter in the first person plural [Federico II Gonzaga to Castiglione?], early 1524, f. 68r
texts.summary: A 'we' told not to ride out feigns illness: rode a horse and schooled a jennet and made a show of being hurt, then sent the physicians urine dyed with blood, letting it be known that he had passed blood, so that it could be shown to the Duke of Sessa; 'but in truth we are as sound and vigorous as we ever were'. Benzoni's life of Federico II tells the same deception, admitted to Castiglione.

texts.label: Capino de Capo, Robbio, 8 April 1524, f. 198r
texts.summary: News from the Lombard campaign: the enemy gone into Novara, skirmishes, Giovanni de' Medici's taking of a bridge; in cipher, if the Spanish truce does not come first, this army will withdraw from river to river, and then into Pavia, Cremona and Milan, according to Bourbon.
